title: Phased arrays, wire antennas and ground
blurb: Predict array patterns from spacing and phase, recognize common wire antennas, and see how ground height, slope and seawater change takeoff angle.

E9C01.why: Half-wave spacing delays the signal 180° along the axis, and the 180° feed cancels that delay. The signals add **along the axis** and cancel broadside.
E9C01.trap: Broadside is where equal path lengths make in-phase feeds add, not out-of-phase ones.

E9C02.why: A quarter-wave spacing (90° of path) plus a 90° phase shift adds in one direction and cancels in the opposite one: a **cardioid**.

E9C03.why: In phase, the paths are equal broadside so signals add there. Along the axis, half-wave spacing cancels them: **broadside figure-eight**.

E9C04.why: Each extra half wavelength of wire adds lobes, and the major lobes tilt closer to the **wire's axis**.
E9C04.trap: Longer does not mean broadside: lobes swing toward the wire.

E9C05.why: Feeding off center puts the feed point where the impedance stays **similar on several bands**, so one feed line and balun work on all.

E9C06.why: The resistor absorbs the wave arriving at the far end, so there is no reflection: the pattern goes **bidirectional to unidirectional**.
E9C06.trap: It does not change polarization or reflect power back.

E9C07.why: The two wires share the current, so impedance is 4 × the 72 Ω dipole, about **300 Ω**.
E9C07.trap: 72 Ω is an ordinary half-wave dipole, 50 Ω is the coax.

E9C08.why: A folded dipole is a half-wave dipole **with an extra parallel wire** joining its ends.

E9C09.why: The G5RV is a wire antenna **center-fed through a set length of open-wire line**, then a balun and coax.

E9C10.why: A Zepp is a half-wave dipole fed **at one end** instead of the center.

E9C11.why: Seawater is a much better reflector than soil, so **radiation at low angles increases** for a vertical.
E9C11.trap: Poor soil, not seawater, weakens the low-angle signal.

E9C12.why: The extended double Zepp is a **center-fed dipole 1.25 wavelengths long**.

E9C13.why: Lobe angle = arcsin(¼ ÷ height in λ). A higher antenna gives a smaller angle, so the lowest lobe takeoff angle **decreases**.

E9C14.why: Downhill, the ground falls away, so the antenna acts higher on that side and the main lobe takeoff angle **decreases** downhill.
